facts.text: White City earned its name from the white‑colored homes that lined its streets, many of which were prefabricated Sears Catalog houses shipped from the 1904 World's Fair.
Founded in 1859 as a modest farming settlement, White City evolved into a mining community with skating rinks, dance halls, gardens, a brick building, and an elementary school.
In 1904, the St. Louis Mining Company sank the first shaft for its #15 coal mine, marking the start of White City’s mining boom.
The village covers just 1.2 square miles, making it one of the smallest incorporated communities in Illinois.
White City’s waterways drain westward into Cahokia Creek, which flows directly into the Mississippi River.
The town was officially incorporated on June 21, 1907, as a coal‑mining community following the opening of Mine No. 15.
